I’m reviewing the current Save Status View layout to identify why the second status text is centering. Then I’ll explain the exact cause in terms of the current frame/alignment chain. Findings - SaveStatusView.swift centers the second text because read Only Field applies .frame(max Width: .infinity) with no alignment argument. In SwiftUI, that defaults to .center, so the Text is centered inside the expanded frame. - SaveStatusView.swift multiline Text Alignment(.leading) does not control where a single-line Text sits inside its frame. It only controls line alignment within the text container. - SaveStatusView.swift view Alignment is only applied in the second .frame(width :alignment:). For the second text view, width is nil, so this modifier does not change the layout. That means the earlier centered infinite-width frame remains the effective layout behavior. I have stored asset “Brightly_Colored_Fish-512-circle-alpha-full” with dimensions of 512x512. I also stored “Brightly_Colored_Fish-512-circle-alpha-full” @2x with dimensions of 1024x1024. Which version is loaded via a call to Image("Brightly_Colored_Fish-512-circle-alpha-full”)? How is the image version determined? Image(" Brightly _ Colored _ Fish -512 -circle -alpha -full") does not hardcode one specific file variant. It asks the asset catalog for that named image, and the system chooses the best representation for the current environment. For your two stored variants: - 1x: 512x512 - 2x: 1024x1024 the chosen version is determined mainly by display scale: - on a standard 1x display, the 1x image is typically used - on a Retina 2x display, the 2x image is typically used In other words, SwiftUI/AppKit resolves the asset by: 1. asset name 2. current trait/environment 3. display scale (NSScreen .backing Scale Factor on macOS, effectively) So if your Mac is running on a Retina display, Image(" Brightly _ Colored _ Fish -512 -circle -alpha -full") will normally render from the @2x representation.
